## Testing Mode
GREEN

## Story DD Coverage
This task is responsible for satisfying the following story done definitions:
- DD1: `docs/orphan-task-convention.md` exists and documents: (a) definition of orphan task, (b) required tag `orphan:deferred_review`, (c) when the orchestrator creates them (DEFER ruling), (d) lifecycle: how they get picked up in future sprints, (e) validate-issues.sh exemption behavior
- DD3: An interim consumer plan is included in the convention doc: how existing callers that produce orphan tasks (if any) should migrate to the new tagging scheme; list known consumers from a grep
- DD4: The doc passes the CLAUDE.md bloat criteria: it contains no architectural implementation details that belong in SKILL.md, no duplicate rules, and no onboarding-only content

## TDD Requirement
test-exempt: Unit exemption criterion 3 — static assets only / non-executable Markdown documentation file. No conditional logic; any test would be a change-detector (existence check). Per behavioral-testing-standard.md Rule 5, non-executable instruction files cannot be deterministically tested for behavioral correctness.

Structural verification is via file existence and content structure checks (grep for required sections).

## Implementation Steps

1. Create `docs/orphan-task-convention.md` at repo root's docs directory.
2. The document must contain all of the following sections:

   ### (a) Definition
   An orphan task is a ticket created by the sprint orchestrator when the cycle-end arbiter issues a `DEFER` ruling for a review finding. These tickets capture review findings that are not BLOCK-worthy (would not prevent merging) but should not be silently dropped — they are deferred to a future sprint for re-evaluation.

   ### (b) Required tag
   Every orphan task created via the DEFER ruling path MUST carry the tag `orphan:deferred_review`. This tag is the primary identifier distinguishing arbiter-created orphan tasks from other parentless tickets.

   ### (c) When created (DEFER ruling)
   The orchestrator creates an orphan task when: (1) the cycle-end arbiter has run, (2) a review finding receives a `DEFER` ruling (not `BLOCK`, not `DROP`), (3) the orchestrator creates a ticket with title "Deferred review finding: <finding summary>", parent=epic, tag=`orphan:deferred_review`. The ticket ID is logged to the cycle ledger entry.

   ### (d) Lifecycle
   - Orphan tasks are created at cycle-end with status=open (or pending).
   - They appear in `ticket list` output by default (not closed, not deleted).
   - Future sprints or maintenance sessions pick them up via `ticket list --tag=orphan:deferred_review` or by reviewing the ticket list at sprint start.
   - When a future sprint addresses the deferred finding: close the orphan task with `--reason="Addressed in sprint <id>: <summary>"` after making the relevant code change.
   - If the deferred finding is no longer relevant, close with `--reason="Obsolete: <reason>"`.

   ### (e) validate-issues.sh exemption
   `validate-issues.sh` health checks flag orphan tickets (tickets with no parent epic) as warnings. Tickets tagged `orphan:deferred_review` are exempted from this health warning because they are intentionally parentless by design — they represent deferred arbiter findings, not accidentally orphaned work. The exemption is scoped to `orphan:deferred_review` only; other orphaned tickets are still flagged. (See S5 / `validate-issues.sh check_orphaned_tasks()` for the implementation.)

   ### Interim Consumer Migration Plan
   As of epic b575-ac1c-f720-4839 (swap-maple-flyby), grep results show no existing callers in `plugins/dso/` that produce `orphan:deferred_review`-tagged tickets. The DEFER ruling ticket creation behavior is being introduced in S5 of this epic.

   Migration path for future callers that create orphan tasks outside the arbiter:
   - Any script or skill that creates a ticket intended as a deferred-review orphan MUST add the `orphan:deferred_review` tag at creation time via `ticket tag <id> orphan:deferred_review`.
   - If a pre-existing script creates parentless tasks for other reasons (e.g., debug-everything standalone bug tickets), it MUST NOT add `orphan:deferred_review` — that tag is reserved for arbiter-deferred findings exclusively.
   - Known callers to audit for tagging compliance: none currently (confirmed by grep `2026-05-16`).

3. Verify the document satisfies CLAUDE.md bloat criteria (Architectural Invariant #2): no architectural implementation details (those belong in SKILL.md or sprint/SKILL.md), no duplicate rules, no onboarding-only content.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] File `docs/orphan-task-convention.md` exists
  Verify: test -f "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/docs/orphan-task-convention.md"
- [ ] Doc contains definition section describing what an orphan task is
  Verify: grep -q "orphan task" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/docs/orphan-task-convention.md"
- [ ] Doc documents required tag `orphan:deferred_review`
  Verify: grep -q "orphan:deferred_review" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/docs/orphan-task-convention.md"
- [ ] Doc explains when the DEFER ruling creates an orphan task
  Verify: grep -qi "DEFER" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/docs/orphan-task-convention.md"
- [ ] Doc documents lifecycle (pickup in future sprints, close conditions)
  Verify: grep -qi "lifecycle\|future sprint\|picked up" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/docs/orphan-task-convention.md"
- [ ] Doc documents validate-issues.sh exemption
  Verify: grep -q "validate-issues" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/docs/orphan-task-convention.md"
- [ ] Doc includes interim consumer migration plan section
  Verify: grep -qi "migration\|consumer" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/docs/orphan-task-convention.md"
- [ ] Doc does not contain inline architectural details that belong in SKILL.md (no phase step descriptions, no internal hook logic, no dispatch plumbing)
  Verify: ! grep -q "Phase [A-Z]\|SubAgent\|dispatch.*sub-agent\|pre-commit hook" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/docs/orphan-task-convention.md"

## Retry Budget
MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3 (sonnet model)
On 3 consecutive sonnet failures: escalate to opus with full diagnostic context (all 3 failure messages)
On 3 consecutive opus failures (6 total): escalate to user with full failure history
If MAX_AGENTS: 0 at sonnet→opus escalation time: skip opus step, escalate to user immediately
